chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Amr ibn Jubayr al-Azrami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

A woman came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband upon the wife?' He said, 'It is more than that.' She said, 'Inform me of something from that.' He said, 'She does not fast (voluntarily) except with his permission.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife fasting voluntarily without her husband's permission in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'tanazzul' (yielding) in marital rights, where the husband’s permission is required for the wife’s voluntary fasting to ensure her duties to him are not neglected. Shia jurists, particularly in the Ja'fari school, distinguish this from obligatory fasting, which does not require his consent, highlighting the balance between spiritual devotion and marital obligations. The narration underscores the husband's role as the head of the household in matters of domestic harmony and resource management.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Amro Bin Jubeyr Al Azramy,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A woman came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so she said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! What is a right of the husband upon the wife?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is a lot from that’. So she said, ‘Inform me with something from that’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is not for her that she should be Fasting except by his permission’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah al-Jamuraniy from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu Hamzah from ‘Amr ibn Jubayr al-‘Arzamiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once a woman came to the Holy prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of a husband on the wife?’
He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘It is more than that.’ She then said, ‘Tell me about a few of them.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘She must not fast without his permission.’”
